name: Sully Balloo's Letter
summary: At the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a dwarf's last words to his wife in Ironforge. Found beneath the bridge, it tells where he died.

sections.title: A Voice from the Riverbed
sections.body: Beneath the stone pilings of the Thandol Span, the land bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands, a drowned skeleton still clutches an envelope. Its water-damaged pages begin, “My dear Sara,” and preserve the tenderness of Sully Balloo's careful writing.

sections.title: The Price of the Span
sections.body: Alliance forces and their enemies have fought fiercely for the Thandol Span. Dark Iron saboteurs and warbands contesting the borderlands have threatened the crossing. Sully Balloo was among the dwarven soldiers sent north to defend it. His family in the mountains knew nothing of his fate until a diver brought his farewell letter up from beneath the waves.

sections.title: A Widow in Ironforge
sections.body: In Ironforge, Sully's widow Sara Balloo receives the letter and learns where her husband died. Grief and lingering hope had left her unsure whether he was missing or lost forever. His handwritten words force her at last to face the bitter truth of his death.

faq.q: Where is Sully Balloo's letter found?
faq.answer: Sully Balloo's Letter was found in a drowned skeleton's hand beneath the stone pillars of the Thandol Span, between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands.

Sully Balloo was an Alliance dwarven soldier who fell defending the Thandol Span. Before taking watch over the span, he wrote a farewell letter to his wife Sara. His remains and the letter were found beneath the icy waters.
Sara Balloo is Sully's widow, living in Ironforge. She has spent months waiting for news of her husband's fate on the northern frontier.

faq.q: What happens after you deliver the letter?
faq.answer: After Sara learns of Sully's death, sorrow overtakes her. She asks that he be memorialized, bringing a further request in Ironforge.

faq.q: Why was the letter still intact underwater?
faq.answer: The envelope clutched in the soldier's remains protected the letter. By the time it was retrieved, the pages were waterlogged and partly dissolved. Enough of Sully's careful writing remained legible to read.

faq.q: What real-world inspiration is behind this quest?
faq.answer: The story honors Major Sullivan Ballou of the 2nd Rhode Island Infantry. Shortly before his death at the First Battle of Bull Run during the American Civil War, he wrote an iconic, poetic farewell letter to his wife.

angles.text: As a dwarf of Ironforge, you honor Sully's final words and a brother-in-arms who died defending the great works of dwarven stonework against northern threats.
As an Alliance soldier, you remember the sacrifices frontline fighters make to protect the fragile overland links between the southern and northern Alliance territories.
